primitives.name: Skating Load
primitives.verbatim_quote: The system as claimed in claim 1 wherein the computing device is programmed to derive work load of an individual over a period of time from the data received from each torso data logger to assess a probability of injury to the individual.
primitives.assumptions: Player workload is proportional to kinetic energy dissipation during skating cycles.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Exceeds baseline threshold L_{skate} > μ + 2σ indicates elevated injury risk.

layer2.mapping: Derived from torso accelerometer and gyroscope data; used as input to GSI's Bayesian injury risk classifier.
layer2.telemetry: Time-series aggregate of kinetic energy per second of activity.

primitives.name: Groin Load
primitives.verbatim_quote: The system as claimed in claim 1 wherein the computing device is programmed to derive groin load from the data from each torso data logger and assess groin load as an indicator of a probability of groin injury for each player.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_{groin}': 'Load magnitude (N·m), integrated rotational stress on pelvic region'}
primitives.assumptions: Groin injury risk correlates with cumulative rotational torque applied to pelvis.
primitives.breakdown_regime: L_{groin} > μ + 3σ signals high probability of groin strain.

layer2.mapping: Computed from torso angular acceleration and hip joint dynamics; feeds into GSI's injury prediction module.
layer2.telemetry: Rotational moment vector at hip joint over time window.

primitives.name: Slap Shot Count
primitives.verbatim_quote: The system as claimed in claim 1 wherein the computing device is programmed to identify and count a number of slap shots executed by each player as a means of assessing the player work load as an indicator of probability of injury for each player.
primitives.assumptions: High-frequency slap shot execution increases muscle fatigue and injury likelihood.
primitives.breakdown_regime: N_{shot} > 10 per game segment implies increased injury risk.

layer2.mapping: Detected via abrupt force spikes in torso data; contributes to total workload metric in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Binary detection of high-force impact events in torso motion profile.
